q: Does real RB actually distinguish a chiral coherent error (e.g. small exp(-i theta Y) rotation) from an achiral Pauli-mixture with matched infidelity, and by how much given a fixed sequence budget?
basis: The paper's central practical selling point beyond group-size economy is sensitivity to real-vs-complex error components. Our replication only injected a real-diagonal (X,Z-only) channel, so the chirality-distinguishing sensitivity was never directly exercised. Standard Clifford RB is known to be insensitive to unitary chirality direction because it averages over the full unitary 2-design.
next_steps: Extend src/real_rb.py to inject two matched-infidelity channels: (a) coherent exp(-i theta Y) with theta chosen so 1 - F_avg = 0.005, (b) an incoherent Pauli mixture with the same 1 - F_avg. Run BOTH standard RB and real RB on each. Report fitted (b, c) pair from the two-exponential real-RB fit (paper eq. 43) and the effective standard-RB decay. Sensitivity metric: |b_chiral - b_achiral| / joint sigma. Free endpoint: local Qiskit-Aer venv already installed.

q: Does the closed-form fitting formula F(m) = A + b^m B + c^m C hold for two-qubit real Clifford RB with a generic (non-diagonal) noise channel, and can b and c be reliably separated at realistic sequence budgets?
basis: For n=1 with real initial state, only the b-branch survives (single exponential). For n>=2 or non-real initial states, the c-branch reactivates and the fit becomes bi-exponential, which is notoriously ill-conditioned. The paper asserts it works; we did not test n=2 nor a mixed-branch scenario at all.
next_steps: Enumerate the n=2 real Clifford group generated by {Z_1, Z_2, H_1, H_2, CZ_{12}}, expected order much smaller than 11520. Build a two-qubit Qiskit circuit with a generic 2-qubit Pauli+coherent noise channel. Fit both branches with scipy curve_fit + a Bayesian bi-exponential prior (or a bootstrap). Report parameter identifiability as a function of M and m_max. Free: local venv.

q: How does an interleaved real-RB variant behave when the interleaved gate is itself outside the real Clifford group (e.g. an S or T gate)?
basis: Standard interleaved RB requires the target gate to be a Clifford. If the interleaved gate is complex Clifford (S) or non-Clifford (T), the theory of interleaved real-RB is unclear: the mixed-group sequence is not a real 2-design and the residual decay may confound gate infidelity with the reference-decay ratio.
next_steps: Formulate the interleaved-real-RB analogue: R g R g R g ... where R is a random real Clifford and g is a fixed target. Simulate for g in {S, sqrt(X), T}. Empirically measure whether the resulting decay is exponential and whether a meaningful g-fidelity estimator can be extracted. Compare against standard interleaved RB on the same g. Free: same venv.

q: Can real RB be extended to matchgate circuits (nearest-neighbor free-fermion circuits), which naturally live in an orthogonal subgroup, and does it give sharper matchgate-error estimation than standard Clifford RB?
basis: Matchgates form a subgroup isomorphic to SO(2n) acting on 2n Majorana modes. Real Cliffords and matchgates share an orthogonal-group structure. If real RB works on the intersection, one might get a native fault-model diagnostic for matchgate architectures (early free-fermion quantum computing hardware, some measurement-based schemes).
next_steps: Read Jozsa-Miyake matchgate group structure; identify matchgate ∩ real Clifford. Simulate a matchgate circuit under both matchgate-native noise (nearest-neighbor XX+YY errors) and generic noise; compare real-RB decay to matchgate-tomography fidelity. Requires implementing matchgate simulator (free: openfermion or hand-rolled Pfaffian sim). No paid endpoint.

q: Can a modern character-RB / cross-entropy-benchmarking (XEB) or ML-based estimator variant reduce the sequence budget of real RB by 3-10x while preserving unbiased b-estimation on realistic non-Markovian noise?
basis: Character RB (Helsen et al.) generalizes RB to arbitrary compact groups by projecting onto irreducible representations; XEB uses porter-thomas statistics; recent neural estimators (2023-2024) have shown wall-clock improvements over curve_fit for standard RB. None of these have been benchmarked head-to-head on real RB specifically, and it is not obvious whether the character-projection route preserves the orthogonal 2-design guarantees.
next_steps: Implement a character-RB estimator over the orthogonal group irreps (trivial + adjoint + sym^2). Compare to (a) curve_fit, (b) a small transformer or GBM regressor trained on simulated (survival-curve -> b) pairs. Metric: RMSE(b) at fixed shot budget. Free endpoints: local venv + Argo Opus for code review.
